Factions, wars and 1.8 raiding physics on 1.21  DominionForge is a factions core for Paper 1.21. It covers claims, power, ranks, diplomacy, scheduled wars, a shared vault, a bank with a ledger, warps and web maps in one plugin. On top of that it has a full 1.8 raiding layer, which stays switched off until you turn it on. 
 Power sets how much land a faction can hold, and it goes down when members stop playing. Wars are declared in advance, so a base isn't taken at 4 a.m. while its builders are asleep.  What sets it apart  
  Power you can check:  base + hours played this week + reputation − recent deaths − inactivity.  /df power  shows every term, so nobody has to ask staff why their number dropped. 
  Scheduled wars:  the attacker declares in advance, the defender gets time to organise, and the attacker only wins by capturing a named objective chunk. 
  Home with a warm-up:   /f home  and warps have a warm-up that breaks if you move or take a hit, plus a combat tag. 
  A vault that can't duplicate items:  everyone looking at the faction chest shares one inventory, saved when the last person closes it. 
  An auditable bank:  every deposit and withdrawal records who, how much and why ( /df bank log ). 
  The raid layer  Everything below ships inside DominionForge and is set per world, with two ready-made profiles (vanilla and 1.8). You edit it from an in-game menu ( /df adminco

Eight skills, sixty abilities and a reason to specialise  SkillsRPG adds eight skills to Paper 1.21 that level from 1 to 100 as players mine, fight, farm and fish. Levels give points to unlock and rank up abilities, which players fire from a three-slot ability bar using mana. Milestone challenges and cross-skill synergies unlock 40 more abilities along the way. It works on the first start with nothing to configure. 
 How it works in play  
  Skills:  Swords, Axes, Archery and Defense for combat; Mining, Woodcutting, Farming and Fishing for gathering. Each one levels from 1 to 100. 
  Abilities:  each skill has four abilities bought with points and ranked up to 5, and four more won in milestone challenges. 64 in total. 
  Ability bar:  three slots, four from total level 200. Press F (swap hands) to switch the active ability and right-click with that skill's tool to fire it. 
  Mana:  50 plus 1 per total skill level, up to 500. It regenerates 5 per second out of combat and shows in a boss bar. 
  Milestones:  a challenge at levels 25, 50, 75 and 100 of every skill, 32 in total. Completing one unlocks that tier's ability. 
  The eight synergies  Reach level 50 in two linked skills and a combined ability unlocks on its own: 
 
 Riposte (Swords + Defense): blocking returns part of the damage. 
 Battle Dance (Swords + Archery): switching between bow and sword stacks damage. 
 Stones

Milestones are skill-specific challenge quests that unlock at skill level thresholds. Completing one grants the player a permanent MILESTONE ability — one that cannot be purchased with points and is never lost during a respec. 
 How milestones work 
 Each skill has  4 milestone tiers : levels  25, 50, 75, and 100 . 
 When a player's skill level crosses one of these thresholds, the corresponding milestone quest  auto-starts  — no command needed. The challenge tab in the GUI hub shows active progress. 
 Once the player meets the condition, the MILESTONE ability for that tier is  automatically granted at rank 1 . The player receives a notification in chat and can immediately equip the ability from the hub. 
 There are  32 milestone abilities  in total (4 per skill × 8 skills). Each grants a permanently accessible passive or active ability themed around what the player accomplished to earn it.

Synergies are a special eighth layer of progression —  8 powerful cross-skill abilities  that reward players who invest across multiple skill trees instead of specializing in one. 
 How synergies work 
 A synergy unlocks  automatically  when a player reaches  level 50 in both qualifying skills . No points required. No quest to complete. The plugin fires a  SkillLevelUpEvent   SynergyGateCheck  — if both required skills are ≥ 50, the synergy ability is granted at rank 1 and the player receives a chat notification. 
 Synergies: 
 
 Cannot be purchased or revoked manually (no admin command to remove them except  /skills admin lock ). 
 Survive a respec — they depend on skill levels, not point allocations. 
 Are equippable to the active ability bar like any other ability. 
 Are lost if skill levels fall below 50 (e.g. via  /skills admin setlevel ).

Quests you write in a file, played through a GUI  QuestForge is a quest plugin for Paper 1.21. You write each quest in a YAML file and players browse, accept and track them from a menu. It supports six objective types, quest chains, daily and weekly repeats, and rewards in money, XP, items and commands. 253 example quests are copied onto your server the first time it starts. 
 How it works in play  
  Quest log:   /quest  opens a menu with the player's active, available and completed quests, with pages for large lists. Hovering a quest shows its description, status and rewards. 
  Accepting:  clicking an available quest asks for a confirmation.  /quest preview <id>  shows the objectives and rewards first. 
  Tracking:  the tracked quest shows its current objective in a boss bar and in the action bar.  /quest track <id>  switches to another quest. 
  Objectives in order:  a quest's objectives run one after another, in the order you wrote them. Progress is saved, so a restart doesn't lose it. 
  Quest givers:  assign quests to a Citizens NPC with  /quest admin npc  and right-clicking it shows only the quests it offers. 
  The six objective types  
  KILL:  a number of a vanilla mob, or a MythicMobs mob with  mythic_mob . 
  COLLECT:  pick up a number of an item. 
  CRAFT:  craft a number of an item. 
  REACH:  get within a radius of a point in a world. 
  TALK:  righ

Shops you edit and reload with players online  ShopForge is a GUI shop plugin for Paper 1.21. Each shop is a YAML file with its own categories, items, buy and sell prices and stock, and  /shop reload  applies changes with players online. Five finished shops with 230 items are copied onto your server the first time it starts, so  /shop  has something to sell straight away.

  Discounts:   shopforge.discount.<percent>  takes that percentage off. If a player has several, the highest one applies. 
  The five shops  Blacksmith (36 items), Farmer's Market (48), Wizard's Tower (48), Quarry (48) and Bazaar (50), each with its own colours, item names and lore. Edit their prices, delete the ones you don't want or use them as templates for your own.  Writing a shop  A shop is one file in  pl

One shared window, and nothing moves until both say yes   TradeForge  is player-to-player trading for  Paper 1.21.x , built around the three decisions that separate a trade window somebody can trust from one that loses items. 
 Two players, one shared window, items and money on the table, and nothing changes hands until both sides have said yes to the same offer.  The three decisions  
  One shared window.  There is exactly one place where a traded stack exists at any moment. Two copies have to be synchronised on every click, and any drift is an item that exists twice or not at all 
  Any change clears both confirmations  — items, money, either side. It is not a setting you can weaken: it is the whole defence against changing the deal after somebody agreed to it 
  All or nothing.  Inventory space and balance are checked for  both  players before anything moves. Handing the goods over and sorting out the leftovers afterwards is how a trade ends with half the load on the floor of somebody else's claim 
  What happens when things go wrong  This is where trade plugins lose items, so it is worth being specific:    Somebody disconnects mid-trade  — what they had on the table is written to disk and handed back the next time they log in. One command claims the chunk you are standing on  ClaimsForge is chunk-based land protection for Paper 1.21. A player stands where they built, runs  /claim , and that chunk is theirs. They can trust friends at four levels, switch PvP, mob spawning and explosions per claim, and manage everything from a menu.

  The menus  
  Your claims  ( /claim list ): every claim you own, with its world, chunk, centre and number of trusted players. Click one to manage it. 
  Manage claim  ( /claim manage ): claim info, trust and untrust, borders, flags and unclaim. Unclaiming asks for confirmation.

  Length is a limit, and it counts what the player SEES.  Formatting codes do not take up space on screen, so they do not count against it. A name past the limit breaks anvils, holograms and hover text, which is why the ceiling exists

Twelve reveal animations and keys that survive anything  CrateForge is a free crate plugin for Paper 1.21. Each crate has one of thirteen reveal animations, shows its key floating above it with a ring of particles in its own colour, and has a pity counter that guarantees a rare prize after a run of bad luck. 
 How it works in play

  Rewards:  items (with enchantments), console commands, Vault money, XP levels and tokens, several in one prize. 
  Keys:  a key is recognised by data stored in the item, so renaming a tripwire hook in an anvil doesn't make one. 
  Getting keys:  votes, commands and mob drops, set per key in its own file.  /cf daily  gives one free key every 24 hours. 
  Broadcasts:  only prizes at or above the rarity you choose are announced to the server. 
  Custom items:  prizes can be Items

The pity system guarantees that players will receive a prize of at least a certain rarity after a configurable number of opens without getting that rarity. It prevents players from going on very long losing streaks. 
 How it works 
 
 Every time a player opens a crate, their  pity counter  increases by 1 
 If the rolled prize meets or exceeds the  guaranteed-min-rarity , the counter  resets to 0  
 If the player reaches the  threshold  without receiving a qualifying prize, the  next open is forced  to roll from prizes of at least  guaranteed-min-rarity  
 After the guaranteed prize is given, the counter resets to 0 
 
  Player opens 49 crates:
  Opens 1-48: Got COMMON prizes. Counter: 1, 2, 3... 48
  Open 49:    Got RARE prize! ✅ Counter resets to 0

Player opens 50+ crates without RARE:
  Opens 1-49: Got COMMON prizes. Counter: 1, 2... 49
  Open 50:    Pity triggers → forced RARE+ prize! 🎰 Counter resets to 0
  
 Configuration 
 The pity system is configured  per-crate  inside the crate's  .yml  file: 
  # Inside crates/legendary.yml

pity:
  enabled: true           # Set to false to disable pity for this crate
  threshold: 50           # After 50 opens without a RARE+, guarantee one
  guaranteed-min-rarity: RARE   # Minimum rarity of the guaranteed prize

Named homes with a menu instead of a command list  SmartHomes is a free homes plugin for Paper 1.21. Players name their homes, give each one an icon and manage them from a menu instead of a list of commands. Overwriting an existing home or deleting one always asks for confirmation first.
